subject: geography
title: US Middle School Geography - Africa
subtitle: Physical environments, regions, settlement, resources, migration, and sustainability across Africa.
description: A source-faithful revision pack on Africa as a diverse continent of regions, climates, physical features, cities, resources, and human-environment relationships. Students practice key terms, compare environments, interpret patterns, and examine case studies including the Nile River, Sahel, Lagos, Congo Basin, and Madagascar.

data.title: Drought and Community Impacts
data.instruction: Put the drought impact chain in the correct order.
items: Lower rainfall occurs.
There is less water in soil, wells, and rivers.
Crops and pasture may struggle.
Food prices may rise and livestock may weaken.
Families and governments make choices.
Possible responses include water conservation, drought-resistant crops, food aid, migration, or improved irrigation.

data.title: How Reliable Water Supports Settlement
data.instruction: Put the settlement explanation in the most logical order.
items: A river or lake provides a more reliable water source than nearby dry land.
People can use the water for drinking, farming, and industry.
Irrigation and fertile land help food production.
Transportation and trade can develop along the water route.
More homes, services, and jobs can grow near the water.
Population density may become higher than in surrounding dry areas.

data.title: Rapid Urban Growth
data.instruction: Put the urban growth process in a logical order.
items: A city offers jobs, trade, education, services, or business opportunities.
People migrate from rural areas or smaller towns.
The city population grows quickly.
Demand increases for housing, transportation, water, electricity, schools, and hospitals.
If infrastructure does not keep up, problems such as traffic, housing shortages, flooding, and waste pressure may increase.
Planning decisions shape whether growth becomes more sustainable and fair.

data.title: Managing a Natural Resource Responsibly
data.instruction: Put the responsible resource-management steps in a logical order.
items: Identify the resource and who depends on it.
Study possible economic benefits such as jobs, exports, income, and infrastructure.
Study possible environmental impacts such as land damage, water pollution, or habitat loss.
Ask how local communities, workers, and public services may be affected.
Create rules for safety, fair benefits, and environmental protection.
Monitor the resource over time so it supports present and future needs.

data.title: Physical, Human, or Human-Environment?

data.title: Challenges and Responses
data.instruction: Sort each statement as a challenge or a response.

pairs.text: Rainfall can be unpredictable in the Sahel.
Droughts can reduce crops and pasture.
Fast city growth can increase housing shortages.
Logging and road building can threaten rainforest habitats.
Planting trees and protecting soil can reduce erosion.
Drought-resistant crops can help farmers adapt.
Better drainage and flood maps can support coastal city planning.
Fair conservation can protect wildlife while considering community needs.
